newsitem.title: USA: Democrats urge Fed not to raise interest rates.
newsitem.headline: Democrats urge Fed not to raise interest rates.

text.p: A group of Democratic lawmakers on Monday urged the Federal Reserve to resist raising interest rates unless there were clear signs inflation was picking up.
The group sent a letter to Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan detailing their concerns two weeks before the Fed's policy-making committee meets on March 25.

The letter from Democratic Sen. Tom Harkin of Iowa, Sen. Byron Dorgan of North Dakota, Sen. Jack Reed of Rhode Island and Representative Maurice Hinchey of New York, opposed a "preemptive strike" against inflation.

"Unless specific and definite signs of inflation can be sighted, we strongly urge you (Greenspan) and the Federal Open Market Committee to resist any action that could lead to higher interest rates," the letter said.
A Fed spokesman had no comment on the letter and said a response would be sent to the lawmakers.

Harkin and a small group of Democrats were instrumental last year in delaying Greenspan's confirmation to another term as Fed chairman. They used the confirmation process to air their criticism that the Fed was standing in the way of stronger economic growth.
The letter also criticised Greenspan's recent characterisation of stock market sentiment as "irrational exuberance," saying his comments had made interest rates rise.
The lawmakers said there were no signs of inflation picking up and that the Fed should consider lowering, not increasing, rates.
"We should fear inflation, we should not fear the ghost of inflation," Harkin said.
